PullRequest.Title: agentHost: publish SDK hook and MCP customization inventory

Refs #343342. Follow-up to #344780.

### Changes

- Consume the selected host's SDK hook and MCP discovery results, including hooks-only and MCP-only plugin contributions.
- Preserve opaque identities, provenance, per-hook enablement, and partial discovery errors. Do not invent file paths or plugin ownership for hooks whose SDK contract supplies neither.
- Merge MCP inventory with live connection state without forwarding native MCP configuration back to the SDK.
- Use SDK-reported MCP enablement as an inherited, non-persistent default, not an instruction to enable or disable a server.
- Show discovered hooks and source-file limitations in the customizations UI.
- Gate explicitly disabled SDK-native MCP servers at create/resume, reconcile host-applied enables and disables back to inheritance, and update passive SDK defaults without persisting host intent.
- Deduplicate nested native MCP contributions, refresh discovery after plugin enablement changes, display MCP discovery diagnostics, and omit source navigation for opaque MCP identities.
- Temporarily recover missing primary-workspace hook actions using an isolated, SDK-backed explicit-directory discovery fallback. See github/copilot-agent-runtime#30644. The fallback never changes execution/trust settings or parses hook files; native repository inventory takes precedence. Source navigation and ownership still require github/copilot-agent-runtime#28553.

No SDK update, client-mode change, enablement migration, or full plugin-forwarding cutover is included. Existing plugin-container parsing remains where the SDK supplies concrete source files.

### Review

The initial two-model review and live Code OSS testing found MCP inheritance/launch gating, nested deduplication, and hook refresh defects. The five inline review comments additionally covered passive SDK defaults, MCP diagnostic visibility, and opaque source navigation.

Addressed in two signed follow-up commits:

- `f626e396fbc` — MCP launch gating, inheritance restoration, passive defaults, and nested deduplication.
- `9718b2dd557` — discovery refresh, MCP diagnostics/navigation, isolated hook compatibility fallback, and CI expectation/regression coverage.

GPT 6.1 Sol reviewed the MCP revision; Claude Opus 5.5 reviewed the discovery/UI revision. Neither found blocking regressions. The fallback is inventory-only: listing a hook does not prove execution or trust eligibility. **Keep draft pending cross-platform validation.**

### Remaining validation

The original [Azure build 490627](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=490627) failed. The relevant provider-integration expectation failures and workspace-hook E2E failure now pass locally. Replacement [Azure build 490654](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=490654) targets `9718b2dd557`, with Windows/Linux/macOS x64 enabled and publishing/release disabled. Packaged Integration Tests (Electron) and Agent Host E2E results are still pending; no cross-platform success is claimed.

Earlier live Code OSS 1.145.0 Dev testing on macOS used an isolated profile, provider home and disposable workspace. It verified UI installation/removal, opaque hook presentation, partial diagnostics, stopped MCP discovery and actual configuration rendering, and exposed the deduplication/refresh defects above. The GUI scenario has not been repeated after these revisions; fixes are covered by the unit and real-provider/AHP tests listed above. No GUI model turn or live MCP connection was exercised.

UI validation used freshly compiled client/Agent Host code and rebuilt built-in extension JavaScript. Full rebuild encountered unrelated Copilot TypeScript-native dependency/export and markdown media type errors; registry E401 prevented dependency restoration, so existing Copilot extension/media artifacts were reused. This limitation does not constitute a full-build pass.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The serial awaits, the second RPC, the critical-path callers, and the runtime gap trigger are all explicit in changed code and tests. Exact milliseconds vary by SDK/runtime and repository contents, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Copilot SDK RPC calls and the hook inventory/filesystem parsing they trigger
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For every customization-discovery anchor and every watched refresh, a workspace whose `.github/hooks` directory exists but whose native result has no repository action performs two hooks-discovery RPCs in sequence; the cost multiplies across live session/chat anchor sets.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked customization/session setup and refresh latency
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Hook inventory was discovered from the watched filesystem inside the existing parallel discovery pass, so this path did not wait for two sequential SDK hook-discovery calls.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new path first awaits `client.rpc.hooks.discover`, then awaits `discoverWorkspaceHooksFallback`; when the runtime's documented repository-hook gap is hit and `.github/hooks` exists, that helper issues and awaits a second `hooks.discover` call before discovery can settle.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 815 newly awaits `discoverWorkspaceHooksFallback` only after the newly added native `hooks.discover` has completed; the fallback's added code performs a second `client.rpc.hooks.discover` for existing workspace hook directories.
Findings.Title: Run the workspace-hook fallback without a serial SDK round trip
Findings.Impact: Opening or resuming a Copilot chat in a repository with workspace hooks, and later refreshing its customizations, now pays an additional full SDK round trip on the critical path. Multiple live sessions or chat anchors repeat the delay independently.
Findings.Evidence: `SessionDiscoveredEntry.whenSettled()` is awaited by `getCustomizationsSettled()` and `getAppliedCustomizations()`, which feed session customization publication and `ActiveClient.snapshot()`. At lines 812-815, the native hooks RPC completes before the fallback starts; lines 879-882 show the fallback makes another SDK RPC. The added integration test establishes the realistic trigger: native discovery returns no workspace hooks while the explicit-directory fallback finds them.
Findings.Recommendation: Probe the workspace hook directory before starting discovery and launch the native and explicit-directory SDK requests concurrently, then preserve the existing ID-based merge and provenance rules; if the SDK can return equivalent inventory/provenance from one request, coalesce them into a single call instead.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial Copilot customization inventory during chat/session publication, create, or resume
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `getCustomizationsSettled()` / `getAppliedCustomizations()` await the anchor's `SessionDiscoveredEntry.whenSettled()` before publication or `ActiveClient.snapshot()` can proceed. The new hook and MCP discovery therefore sit on this critical path; the workspace-hook fallback is serial after native hook discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: SDK `hooks.discover` inventories and parses hook actions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per scan, plus one additional call when an existing workspace hook directory hits the runtime repository-hook gap
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Hook files were discovered through local filesystem traversal; there were no hook-discovery SDK RPCs on this path
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both calls must settle before customization inventory is available; the fallback call starts only after the first finishes

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: SDK `mcp.discover` enumerates MCP servers with effective source metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per scan and effective live anchor
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No MCP SDK inventory call was made by `SessionCustomizationDiscovery`
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in parallel with other discovery but the scan cannot settle until it completes

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve and parse plugin roots/manifests, including roots inferred from MCP effective source files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per distinct discovered plugin root in an anchor scan
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Plugin parsing already occurred for agent/skill-backed roots; this diff additionally allows MCP effective-source files to introduce roots
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after SDK inventories and before the result settles

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One scan per effective live anchor set within a session. Across sessions, identical folder sets are not shared. Hook fallback triggers for each anchor whose primary workspace has an existing hook directory and whose native SDK result contains no repository hook.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Agents, rules, skills, hooks, MCP discovery, and watcher setup run under one `Promise.all`. Within the hook branch, native discovery and fallback discovery are serialized. Different session/anchor scans can run concurrently without a process-wide limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Discovered directory locations are cached after the first scan, but SDK hook and MCP inventories and plugin parsing are recomputed on every scan. Anchor results are reused only within the same session and ordered anchor set.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed awaits, call graph, tests, and runtime-gap integration coverage establish the calls and ordering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK RPC duration varies with runtime state and installed plugin count, but the serial two-call hook path and its critical-path placement are deterministic for the documented trigger.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable latency regression: the compatibility fallback adds a second full SDK hook-discovery round trip serially on a required critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Customization refresh after watched file changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A matching filesystem event invalidates directory discovery, is debounced for 100 ms, and then republishes only after a full discovery scan settles. UI/session inventory refresh waits for that scan, though active model turns do not directly wait on it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Watched file notification followed by directory resolution and plugin/source reads
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full scan per debounced event per affected anchor
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same watcher/debounce mechanism already triggered full agent/rule/skill/hook filesystem discovery
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks publication of refreshed inventory, not the current active turn

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: New SDK hook and MCP discovery during every full refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two new RPC families per scan, with a possible second hooks call
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Refreshes did not invoke SDK hook or MCP inventory
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must settle before the refreshed inventory is published

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Relevant customization file events, coalesced within the 100 ms delayer, multiplied by live anchor sets watching their own roots.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Events within the debounce window coalesce. A newer refresh cancels the wrapper promise for an in-flight scan, while independent anchors refresh concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Directory-location cache is invalidated on a matching event. Hook/MCP inventory has no family-specific cache, so unrelated customization changes also rerun those SDK calls.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for added boundary calls and refresh reachability; medium for user-visible impact outside repositories using workspace hooks.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Save cadence and SDK scan duration vary; debounce bounds normal editor bursts. The serial fallback cost is covered by the submitted finding rather than duplicated.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding beyond the reported serial fallback; ordinary refresh work is debounced and the additional inventories are required for the new feature.

Scenarios.Scenario: Plugin install, uninstall, catalog apply, or enablement change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The management operation awaits runtime mutation, live-session reloads where applicable, and `_refreshDiscoveredCustomizations()` before returning, so refreshed inventory publication is part of the operation latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Plugin list/enable/disable and per-live-session plugin reload
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Plugin list twice and one mutation once, then one reload per live session
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Plugin enablement already performed list/mutation verification and reloaded live sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All are awaited by the plugin enablement operation

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh all discovered customization inventories, including new hook/MCP SDK calls
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One scan per already-instantiated live anchor across active sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Plugin enablement did not explicitly refresh discovered inventories; install/uninstall/catalog paths already did
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the management operation returns

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All active session clients times all live anchor sets that have already started discovery. The added enablement path is explicitly tested with two sessions and an extra peer anchor.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Live session reloads run concurrently, then discovery refresh runs across active clients and anchors with `Promise.all`; each anchor internally launches its discovery RPCs concurrently except for the hook fallback.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cross-session or cross-anchor coalescing exists. Same-session chats sharing an exact anchor set reuse one entry; undiscovered anchors are skipped by explicit refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for fan-out and awaiting behavior; lower that the bounded, user-initiated fan-out independently causes material degradation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most users keep few simultaneous sessions/peer anchors, and plugin mutations are infrequent. Larger active-session counts increase the burst, but the all-anchor refresh is necessary to update globally affected plugin contributions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the refresh is an intentional consistency cost, bounded by live discovered anchors, and evidence does not justify a separate performance defect.

Scenarios.Scenario: Live MCP enablement reconciliation during launch, turn preparation, status changes, and host override restoration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Turn preparation awaits `mcp.listConfigured()` and any required enable/disable RPCs before sending. Status-change handling may refresh configured inventory; metadata-only publication does not itself block model execution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same inventory call already occurred before desired-state reconciliation
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks MCP reconciliation and turn preparation

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Session MCP enable/disable to apply or restore host decisions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one mutation per server whose desired and observed states differ in a reconciliation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Enable/disable calls already existed; the diff extends one-time restoration to host-enabled SDK-native servers and avoids projecting passive defaults as intent

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured MCP server count and the subset whose observed state differs from an explicit host decision or requires one-time inheritance restoration.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The configured inventory is fetched once per reconciliation; enable/disable mutations are awaited sequentially in the existing loop and per-server lifecycle controls use sequencing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Runtime states and observed defaults are held in session maps. The new host-applied enablement map is session-lifetime bounded and looked up by server name; no collection-wide external cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call sites and state guards show mutations remain mismatch-driven and bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Server counts and runtime mutation duration vary, but changed logic does not create per-event toggling when state already matches.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: the diff changes decision semantics and metadata overlays but does not increase steady-state boundary cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Customization and MCP list UI refresh
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Customization change notifications synchronously rebuild the discovery status text and filter installed servers before optional relayout; there are no new network, IPC, or filesystem operations in this callback.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Published customization count and MCP list membership per customization notification.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Runs synchronously on the UI event callback; gallery fetching remains separately gated and unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The message is recomputed from current in-memory customizations and DOM text is only replaced when changed. Opaque hooks now bypass file reads during expansion.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for in-memory-only behavior and absence of changed expensive boundaries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Inventory sizes are typically small; no evidence shows enough rows or notification frequency for the added linear scan to cause jank.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: added UI work is a bounded linear scan, and skipping unreadable hook files avoids filesystem work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 28 changed files and traced customization discovery, plugin mutation refresh, session launch/MCP reconciliation, and customization UI updates. Submitted one medium-confidence-in-magnitude, high-confidence-in-mechanism latency finding for the serial workspace-hook fallback RPC. Other new work is bounded by live anchors or discovered inventory and did not establish an additional actionable regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
